followup_reviews.Research finding: Retain two distinct evidentiary phases: a 2–3 July 2021 announced interruption and the later reported freight restoration on 9 July. They do not establish one continuous closure from 2 to 9 July. The operational report concerns road freight and clearance toward Botswana/Namibia, with reopening limited to 06:00–18:00. The SARS schedule does not enumerate every cohort or direction. No complete passenger or all-direction prohibition is inferred. P1 remains an unverified 11:00–06:00 intended window with no operational duration. P2 has a reported 9 July restoration and unknown onset. Eight weeks of constrained services is not eight weeks of continuous closure; both numeric durations and complete/exact operational flags remain withheld. Temporary service suspension is attributed to the stated shortage of port-health officials. The involvement of a health service does not automatically make the rationale disease control, and the reporter’s criticism is not coded as the authority’s purpose. SARS and the 9 July Freight News article were freshly read; the 8 July indexed report remains a cached prospective account from the same reporter/publisher lineage. This researcher authored original R06, so this is an openly disclosed re-audit requiring separate challenge. The frozen rows are unlocated; the separately accepted B02 replacement rows match their guards and PIDA S21, -25.27550 / 25.71349. Preserve the freight scope and unspecified direction. P1 is an announced-window layer; P2 is dated evidence only. Neither point locates an exact health office or barrier.
